title: Abrams: Iron on the Horizon
direction: Original instrumental armour-combat score: low French horns, analogue sequencer, dark cello ostinati, dry military snare, warm electric piano, acoustic space. A human crew inside a formidable machine. Distinctive, restrained, late-Cold-War electronic-orchestral character. No artist imitation, sampled game music, vocals, chants, speech, gunshots or radio effects.
motif: Five notes D A F E D, shaped long-short-short-short-long. Assertive in the menu, fragmented in combat, softened in idylls, distorted after friendly fire, resolved in the final homecoming. This is a composition request; generated pitch fidelity requires listening verification.
generation_policy: Use existing account credits only. Twelve masters, choose one of each generated pair. No subscription change, extra credit purchase, audio upload or public publishing. Preserve original downloads unchanged; create game-ready derivatives separately.

tracks.title: 01 Iron on the Horizon
tracks.prompt: Instrumental main-menu theme for Abrams, an M1 tank game. Original cinematic late-Cold-War electronic-orchestral score, D minor, 96 BPM, 4/4. Memorable five-note French-horn hook D A F E D, long-short-short-short-long. Solid analogue bass pulse, dry snare, deep toms, cello eighth notes, burnished horns and a thin glassy synth line. Weight, discipline, danger and the humanity of four crew members. Strong identifiable melody within the first ten seconds, elegant B section, return to the hook. Three-minute game soundtrack, clear inner detail, controlled bass, no huge trailer drops. Instrumental only, no voices, no choir, no combat sound effects. Begin on the pulse and end on a sustained dominant suitable for an edited loop.
tracks.arrangement:
[Instrumental]
[Intro: low pulse, horn motif]
[A: strings join, disciplined snare]
[B: open space, electric piano answers]
[A: full warm horns, controlled lift]
[Loop tail: dominant pedal, no final crash]

Continuous pulse, even ending for an edited loop.
tracks.arrangement:

[Orders: muted strings, horn fragment]
[Consideration: warm suspended chords]
[Return: piano, unchanged pulse]

tracks.title: 09 Blue on Blue
tracks.prompt: Instrumental friendly-fire consequence cue for a tank game. Bleak doom-laden orchestral judgement, D minor with a flattened second, 52 BPM. One immediate low brass dissonance, bowed contrabass, a single dark tolling bell, slow heavy tom heartbeat, fractured descending D A F E D theme. Shock, guilt, dread, irreversible harm to one's own side. Accusatory and human, with cold empty space. Sixty seconds: ominous recognition, spare development, dying unresolved final chord. This is a consequence, never a reward. No triumphant action groove, metal riff, vocals, choir, spoken verdict, gunfire, scream or film sound effects. Powerful low register at controlled volume.
tracks.arrangement:

Intimate loss and stillness, restrained dignity, no sentimental swell. Sixty to ninety seconds with an immediate short sombre opening and a complete quiet ending. No horror jump scare, combat sounds, voices, breath, choir or military funeral quotation. Keep low-level detail audible without loudness maximisation.
